narrative.overview:
The system is built for reading evidence. A ledger of production deploys sits on the page, and its annotation is written above it in plain words: one sentence in large navy type gives the answer, short claims give the reasons, and each claim links down to the row that proves it. Figures come after the words, and a period's figures always stand next to the period before. Every device on the page either states a fact or shows where the fact came from.

The material is Cloudnonic's own and deliberately plain: navy on a cool paper grey and white, Manrope for every glyph, 1px navy-tinted hairlines in place of boxes and shadows. The density is that of a well-kept table: one loud line, then a tight ladder from 11 to 17px where the evidence lives. Colour is spent on meaning only: navy for what a reader acts on, green, amber and red for state, a pale navy wash for whatever is linked or has just been reached, and a hatch where data is missing.

It is an internal tool for people who come back after every deploy, so nothing is there to impress. Motion is a 150ms colour change; the one authored moment is the highlight a row plays when a claim's link lands on it. The board holds to WCAG 2.1 AA, never carries state by colour alone and respects reduced motion. Confirmed rejection: the KPI-tile dashboard and its card grids; figures live in rows and in the period rail.
keyCharacteristics: Words before numbers: one navy sentence at display size answers the page, and no metric is set above 15px.
Cloudnonic navy on paper grey and white, with the Cloudnonic cloud mark and Manrope as binding identity.
A flat ledger: a tone step from ground to white and 1px navy-tinted hairlines, never a shadow.
Three state colours, each always paired with an icon and words; missing data is hatched and named.
Watch windows drawn as 72-hour timelines with the 24 h mark at one third.
Tabular figures only where figures stack.
Motion is colour; the row arrival is the only authored moment.

rules.name: The Navy Voice Rule
rules.body: Navy is the only brand colour and there is no second accent. What a reader should act on or remember is navy; everything else is a navy-tinted grey or a state.

rules.name: The Three States Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean clean, watching and failed, and nothing else. They colour text, icons and timeline strokes on the surface they sit on, always next to an icon and words.

rules.name: The Hatched Absence Rule
rules.body: Missing data is drawn as a hatch (1px Navy Rule stripes at 135 degrees, every 6px) and named "No data". It is never drawn as zero, an empty track or a grey bar.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Manrope sets every glyph: the verdict, figures, times and versions (tags or SHAs). There is no monospace; a version is a name, set at 13px medium beside its service.

rules.name: The Stacked Figures Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures and short units ("68 h", "2.4 d") are only for figures that stack: verdict labels, period values, the 0/24/72 h scale. Inside sentences figures stay proportional, units are spelled out ("68 hours of its watch left") and small counts are words ("two new errors").

rules.name: The Words Over Numbers Rule
rules.body: Display size belongs to a sentence that answers the page's question, never to a number on its own. No metric on the board is set above 15px.

rules.name: The Inset Highlight Rule
rules.body: Anything that can be highlighted carries 12px of horizontal padding, so the wash never touches its text. Rows sit 12px inside their list; claims pull their padding outward with a negative margin, so their text keeps the column edge.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no lifts. A surface separates from the ground by turning white and taking a 1px navy-tinted hairline, and a row separates from its neighbour by a hairline alone.

rules.name: The Containment Radius Rule
rules.body: Radius follows what an element contains: 12px for panels, 8px for blocks, 6px for controls, 4px for the smallest shapes, including anything inside a control. Round caps belong only to the timeline's strokes and ticks.

rules.name: The Colour-Not-Movement Rule
rules.body: Interaction changes colour, never position or size. The only movement is a 0.97 press on the org segments, and only when the reader has not asked for reduced motion; the only authored moment is the row arrival.

rules.name: The Linked Highlight Rule
rules.body: A claim and its row are one thing in two places. Pointing at either one, or focusing the claim's link, washes both in Navy Wash; following the link lands on the row with the arrival highlight.

rules.name: The 72-Hour Window Rule
rules.body: Every watch is drawn on the same 72-hour line with its 24 h mark at one third, so windows compare by eye down a column: elapsed time in the state colour, events as red ticks, absence as hatch.

dos: Do set pages on Paper Grey (#f7f7f7) and keep Sheet White (#ffffff) for the header bar, contained panels and controls.
Do answer in a sentence first: Display type in navy (700, 2.5rem from 1024px, -0.025em, line-height 1.1, balanced), with every claim linked to the row that proves it.
Do pair every state colour with its Phosphor bold icon and words: check circle for clean, eye for watching, warning circle for failed, prohibit for no data.
Do draw missing data as the hatch and name it "No data"; an open window reads "Watching, N h left", never zero.
Do use tabular figures and short units only where figures stack: verdict labels, period values, the time scale.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better on Paper Grey, Sheet White and Navy Wash; Faded Slate on Navy Wash (4.78:1) is the lowest pair in use.
Do show focus as a 2px solid navy outline at 2px offset.
Do keep transitions to colour, 150ms on the ease-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)); put any press scale (0.97) behind motion-safe and leave the arrival highlight static under reduced motion.
donts: Don't build KPI tiles or card grids; figures live in rows and in the period rail, where each current value sits over the previous period's.
Don't give a number display size; no metric is set above 15px.
Don't introduce a monospace face for versions, SHAs or times.
Don't add shadows; separate with a tone step and a 1px navy-tinted hairline.
Don't add a second accent hue, or use green, amber or red for anything but state.
Don't carry state by colour alone.
Don't draw missing data as zero, an empty track or a blank cell.
Don't move or resize anything on hover or focus; interaction changes colour.
